content.text: {"relation":"MATCH","consensus_summary":"All four blind responses identify 'the Lamb' as Jesus Christ in his role as the sacrificial, atoning offering for sin — the unblemished 'Lamb of God' fusing the Passover lamb, the Levitical sacrifices, and Isaiah's suffering servant, culminating in Revelation's slain-yet-victorious, enthroned Lamb who redeems and reigns. Alternatives (warrior-lamb background, lambs as believers, servant/talya readings, Tamid background) are noted but do not displace this core.","book_summary":"The book identifies the Lamb as Jesus Christ — the unblemished Passover sacrifice, slain to redeem His people and now reigning, citing Exodus 12:5, Isaiah 53:7, John 1:29, 1 Corinthians 5:7, 1 Peter 1:18-19, and Revelation 5:6-13.","consensus_core_identification":"Jesus Christ as the sacrificial, unblemished, atoning Lamb (Passover/servant typology) who was slain for sin and now reigns victorious in Revelation.","book_core_identification":"Jesus Christ as the unblemished Passover sacrifice, slain to redeem His people, now reigning.","core_relation":"EQUIVALENT","extension_relation":"SAME_CASES","boundary_disagreement":"None of substance. The book foregrounds the Passover-lamb background specifically ('unblemished Passover sacrifice'), while the consensus treats Passover as one of several fused backgrounds (Passover, Levitical cult, Isaiah 53, Akedah). But the book also cites Isaiah 53:7, so it does not exclude the servant background; this is emphasis, not a boundary change. The book's 'to redeem His people' could be read slightly more particularistically than John 1:29's 'sin of the world,' but Revelation 5:9's 'out of every kindred, and tongue, and people, and nation' — which the book cites — covers the same universal scope the consensus describes.","material_contradiction":"None. Every element of the book's entry (unblemished, Passover, sacrificial, slain, redemptive, reigning) is affirmed by all four consensus responses.","rationale":"The book's core identification — Jesus Christ as the slain, unblemished, redemptive Passover Lamb now reigning — is precisely the primary meaning stated in all four blind responses, including the paradoxical sacrifice-plus-kingship synthesis from Revelation 5. The citation set is nearly identical to the consensus's primary basis (Ex 12, Isa 53:7, John 1:29, 1 Cor 5:7, 1 Pet 1:18-19, Rev 5). Differences are limited to wording and which OT background is named first, which the consensus itself flags as an intramural emphasis question rather than a disagreement about the referent. No extension is added, excluded, or reclassified.","citation_support":"STRONG","strongest_objection":"One could argue the book narrows the typological background to the Passover lamb specifically ('the unblemished Passover sacrifice'), whereas the consensus presents a broader fusion of backgrounds (Levitical offerings, Tamid, Akedah, servant), potentially making this a mild REFINED narrowing of emphasis; however, the book's inclusion of Isaiah 53:7 and Revelation 5 shows it embraces the same composite picture, so the objection reduces to wording.","confidence":"high"}
